blockMcqs.question: What does X → Y (X determines Y) mean?
options: Y rows always sort after X rows
Rows matching on X must also match on Y
X and Y must be in separate tables
Y is always a subset of X
blockMcqs.explanation: X → Y means any two rows that agree on every attribute in X must agree on every attribute in Y.

blockMcqs.question: Which FD is trivial?
options: {A,B} → C
A → B
{A,B} → A
A → {B,C}
blockMcqs.explanation: {A,B} → A is trivial because A is already part of {A,B}, so Y ⊆ X. It can never be violated.

blockMcqs.question: Armstrong's augmentation rule states that if X → Y then:
options: Y → X also holds
X → YZ holds for any Z
XZ → Y holds for any Z
XZ → YZ holds for any Z
blockMcqs.explanation: Augmentation: if X → Y then adding the same attributes Z to both sides gives XZ → YZ.

blockMcqs.question: If X → YZ holds, what can you always derive?
options: Y → Z and Z → Y
X → Y and X → Z separately
YZ → X
X → Y only if Z is a key
blockMcqs.explanation: Decomposition: if X → YZ then X → Y and X → Z each hold independently.

blockMcqs.question: When does X⁺ (attribute closure of X) equal a superkey?
options: When X⁺ contains X itself
When X⁺ covers all attributes in the schema
When X has only one attribute
When X appears on every FD right-hand side
blockMcqs.explanation: X is a superkey when its closure X⁺ = the full set of attributes, meaning X determines everything.

blockMcqs.question: In the closure algorithm, when do you stop expanding the result set?
options: After processing each FD exactly once
When every FD has been applied
When the result set stops changing
After adding all attributes on the right-hand sides
blockMcqs.explanation: The algorithm is a fixed-point iteration — stop when no new attributes can be added in a full pass.

blockMcqs.question: Which property is NOT required for a minimal cover?
options: Every RHS is a single attribute
No redundant FD exists
No extraneous LHS attribute exists
Every LHS is a single attribute
blockMcqs.explanation: A minimal cover requires single-attribute RHS and no redundancy/extraneous LHS attributes — the LHS can still be a set of attributes.

blockMcqs.question: An attribute that never appears on any FD right-hand side must be:
options: Excluded from every candidate key
On every candidate key
A primary key on its own
Extraneous in every FD
blockMcqs.explanation: If A never appears on an RHS, nothing determines A, so it cannot be derived from other attributes — it must appear in every candidate key.
